analysis: The code snippet calls Signature.getInstance(ALGO) without any prior validation or null check on the ALGO constant. The method signature declares two exceptions: NoSuchAlgorithmException (checked) and NullPointerException (unchecked). There is no check to ensure that ALGO is not null or that it is a supported algorithm name. Although the code catches NoSuchAlgorithmException (along with SignatureException and InvalidKeyException) and rethrows as CryptoException, the exception condition is not avoided—it is merely handled. NullPointerException is not caught at all. Therefore, both exceptions remain possible in this context.
answer: NoSuchAlgorithmException: not avoided. NullPointerException: not avoided.
remark: NoSuchAlgorithmException is triggered if the algorithm represented by ALGO is not supported by any registered security provider. This can occur if ALGO is an invalid or misspelled algorithm name. NullPointerException is triggered if ALGO is null. Since the code does not perform any null check or algorithm validation before calling getInstance, both exceptions can occur.
